 NHL On Tap: Schaefer can stretch home point streak for Islanders vs. Kings
 Mammoth look to keep rolling; Hurricanes, Oilers set to square off
 © 
 Bruce Bennett/Getty Images
 By 
 NHL.com 
 @NHLMedia 
 October 22, 2026 
 Link copied 
 There are 12 games on the NHL schedule Thursday, including two televised nationally in the United States. Here are five things to watch today, along with the complete game schedule. 
 Schaefer hot at home 
 Matthew Schaefer will try to extend his season-opening home point streak to six games when the New York Islanders host the Los Angeles Kings in the first game of an ESPN+ doubleheader (7:30 p.m. ET; Disney+, HULU, ESPN+, SN+). Schaefer has seven assists through his first five games at UBS Arena, where the Islanders are 4-1-0 this season. New York (5-3-1) is 3-0-1 in its past four games overall. Los Angeles (1-4-2) continues a five-game road trip after defeating the Washington Capitals 5-2 in the opener Tuesday to earn its first win of the season. Kings coach Peter Laviolette, who had his first NHL coaching job with the Islanders (2001-03), can move within one of Ken Hitchcock (849) for sixth in League history with his 848th career win.
 ANA@NYI: Holmstrom redirects Schaefer's shot for PPG
 Mammoth start 
 The Utah Mammoth will try to at least maintain a hold of first place in the Central Division when they visit the Seattle Kraken (10 p.m. ET; Disney+, HULU, ESPN+, SN+). Utah (7-3-0) has won four of its past five games (4-1-0) and is tied with the Minnesota Wild atop the Central. The Mammoth have had 18 players score at least one goal this season, which is most in the NHL. The Kraken (6-3-1) are also off to a strong start and play the second game of a four-game homestand they opened with a 4-3 shootout win against the Detroit Red Wings on Tuesday. The Kraken are tied with the Vegas Golden Knights with 12 multigoal-scorers.
 Heavyweight matchup 
 The reigning Stanley Cup champion Carolina Hurricanes visit the Edmonton Oilers for a showdown between two of the NHL’s top teams (9 p.m. ET: TVAS, SNW, CARNHL, HHN). Carolina (8-2-1) leads NHL with 17 points and has won eight of its past nine games (8-1-0). Edmonton (7-1-1) is second in the Western Conference and Pacific Division with 15 points, one behind Vegas (8-3-0) with two fewer games played. Captain Connor McDavid , who leads the NHL with 26 points (six goals, 20 assists) and has three four-point games this season, can join Mario Lemieux (three times), Mike Bossy and Wayne Gretzky as the only players in League history to reach 30 points in 10 games or fewer. Seth Jarvis will be a game-time decision to make his season debut for the Hurricanes after recovering from offseason shoulder surgery. The forward, who led Carolina with 32 goals in each of the past two seasons, was activated from the injured non-roster list Wednesday.
 EDM@UTA: McDavid scores his second goal of the game
 Shipping back to Boston 
 The Atlantic Division-leading Boston Bruins return home from a 3-0-1 road trip to host the Nashville Predators (7 p.m. ET; SCRIPPS, NESN). The Bruins (7-2-1) are 5-0-1 in their past six games, sparked by forward James Hagens , who is tied with forwards Trevor Connelly of the Golden Knights and Ivar Stenberg of the San Jose Sharks for the NHL rookie scoring lead with seven points (three goals, four assists) in 10 games. Nashville (3-2-3) will try to win consecutive games for the first time this season following a 5-2 victory against the St. Louis Blues on Saturday. Steven Stamkos has points in seven of the Predators’ first eight games and the forward leads them with 10 (four goals, six assists). He is two away from joining Alex Ovechkin (476) and Sidney Crosby  (306) as the only active NHL players with 300 road goals.
 Last stop before Jet-ting outdoors 
 The Winnipeg Jets will play their final game before hosting the 2026 Tim Hortons NHL Heritage Classic when they visit the Dallas Stars (8 p.m. ET; KDFW 4, Prime Video, TSN3). Forward Kyle Connor , who is tied for second in the League with eight goals, will try to help Winnipeg (4-3-2) end a 0-2-1 slide. Dallas (5-3-1) will seek its fourth straight win. Stars forward Jason Robertson (216 goals, 283 assists in 465 games) needs one point to reach 500 for his NHL career. The Jets will head home afterward to take on the Montreal Canadiens outdoors at Princess Auto Stadium on Sunday. Winnipeg will become the second Canada city to host two NHL outdoor games; Edmonton hosted the Heritage Classic in 2003 and 2023.
